course.title: AI at Work: Think Clearly, Work Responsibly
course.description: A three-level, hands-on pathway for using AI responsibly in defense, civilian, space, and business work.
course.audience: Professionals across defense, civilian, space mission, and business functions
course.promise: Finish with a repeatable method for turning a work task into an AI-assisted result you can stand behind.

clearSteps.name: Clarify
clearSteps.description: Define the audience, outcome, and success criteria before you open an AI tool.

clearSteps.name: Limit
clearSteps.description: Choose appropriate information, tools, and decision boundaries for the task.

clearSteps.name: Engineer
clearSteps.description: Give the model a clear role, relevant source material, constraints, and an output format.

clearSteps.name: Assess
clearSteps.description: Test important claims, assumptions, omissions, tone, and fit for the real audience.

clearSteps.name: Refine
clearSteps.description: Revise with judgment, document what matters, and keep a human accountable for the result.

levels.name: Beginner
levels.title: Use AI with confidence
levels.description: Learn the CLEAR habits for framing work, protecting information, prompting well, checking output, and keeping human ownership.
levels.audience: Employees beginning to use approved AI tools for everyday workplace tasks
levels.outcome: Create a useful AI-assisted result that is safe, grounded, reviewed, and owned.

levels.name: Intermediate
levels.title: Build reliable AI workflows
levels.description: Move from one-off prompts to decomposed, risk-based, traceable workflows that teams can review and reuse.
levels.audience: Practitioners, team leads, analysts, engineers, and functional professionals designing repeatable AI-assisted work
levels.outcome: Build a multi-step workflow with controlled inputs, source traceability, human gates, and a reusable handoff.

levels.name: Advanced
levels.title: Govern and scale AI systems
levels.description: Design operating models, enforce governance boundaries, evaluate and challenge systems, assure human control, and scale through evidence.
levels.audience: AI program owners, product and platform leads, governance partners, technical authorities, and senior functional leaders
levels.outcome: Make a defensible lifecycle decision for an AI system using value, risk, evaluation, control, and operations evidence.
